task.description:
WF-03 Step 4 -- write the regression coverage for the ISS-0106 fix. WF-03's Step 4 rule is stricter than WF-02's: the test must be shown to FAIL against pre-fix code and PASS against post-fix code, and you must state that explicitly in the test spec. A test that only ever ran against already-fixed code proves nothing about whether it covers the bug.

THE FIX HAS THREE PARTS AND THEY NEED DIFFERENT TREATMENT. Read the design at lib/letflow/design/iss0106-toolchain-pin-and-format-fix.md for the full specification.

  PART A -- a NEW mix task, lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain.ex, which reads .tool-versions and prints an advisory toolchain warning. **This is the only genuinely new executable surface in the run and it is where your test effort belongs.** It has never had a test.

  PARTS B and C -- four files reformatted, and sixteen struct-update bind-site annotations. **Do NOT write ExUnit tests for these.** Their regression guard already exists and is already an exit-code gate in the `letflow.check` alias: `mix format --check-formatted` and `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`. Writing an ExUnit test that re-asserts what an existing exit-code gate already enforces would be duplicated machinery, and core-directives.md prefers exit-code gates precisely because they cannot be satisfied by renaming something. Instead, RECORD the fail-then-pass evidence for B and C in the spec, citing the measurements already made in this run: both gates exit 1 on pre-fix code and 0 on post-fix code. Verify those exit codes yourself at the two commits rather than quoting the claim -- `main` is the pre-fix state and HEAD is post-fix.

WHAT PART A's TESTS MUST COVER. Derive the list from the design and the module, not from this paraphrase, but at minimum: the MATCH path; the MISMATCH path (both the Elixir mismatch and the OTP mismatch, and the case where both mismatch); the OTP comparison's major-only rule, which is the subtle one -- a pinned `erlang 29.0.5` must MATCH a running OTP release of `29`, and a naive full-string comparison would report a permanent false mismatch on a correctly-pinned host; the `-otp-NN` suffix being stripped from the elixir token and not participating in the OTP verdict; the parse contract (comment lines, blank lines, other tools' lines, malformed lines); and every failure mode the design enumerates as F1..F8 (missing file, empty file, no elixir line, no erlang line, malformed line, unreadable file). For every one of these, `run/1` must return `:ok` and must not raise -- that is the property the whole option was made conditional on, so assert it, do not assume it.

THREE HAZARDS SPECIFIC TO TESTING THIS MODULE:

  1. **Its only public function is `run/1`, and it reads `.tool-versions` from the current working directory.** Every helper is private. So a test cannot call the parser or the comparison rule directly -- it must drive the whole task with a controlled cwd, and capture stderr. Plan for that: a test that changes cwd cannot be `async: true`, and stderr capture needs `ExUnit.CaptureIO.capture_io(:stderr, fn -> ... end)`. If you conclude the module genuinely cannot be tested to the depth these criteria require without a public seam, REPORT THAT as a finding rather than inventing one or writing a weaker test -- adding a public function is a design change and would route back through CODE-DESIGNER, not through you.

  2. **Do NOT write a test that asserts what THIS host's toolchain happens to be.** A test that passes only on Elixir 1.20.3/OTP 29 would fail on the hetzner host or any host that later moves, which would turn this fix into a new cross-host breakage -- the precise class of problem ISS-0106 is about. Every assertion must be driven by a fixture `.tool-versions` you control, compared against the running toolchain read at runtime, never against a hardcoded version string.

  3. **ExUnit hard-caps `"test " <> describe <> " " <> test_name` at 255 characters and exceeding it is a compile-time SystemLimitError that fails the ENTIRE suite, not one test.** docs/anti-patterns.md records four separate occurrences of this exact class in this project. Keep combined describe+test names comfortably under 200 characters, put the spec citation in a `#` comment above the test rather than in the name string, and RUN A MECHANICAL LENGTH CHECK over every describe/test pair you write, quoting the maximum you measured. The anti-pattern entry explicitly says documentation alone has not been sufficient to prevent recurrence, so measure rather than eyeball.

WRITE THE SPEC to test/specs/ISS-0106.md and the test code to test/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain_test.exs (create the directory if needed -- check where an existing mix-task test lives first, since lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex already has one, and follow that placement convention rather than inventing a new one).

You write the tests; you do NOT run the full suite as your gate -- TEST-RUNNER owns that at the next step. But you must run your OWN new tests, and you must produce the fail-first evidence, so running is expected. Do NOT run `docker compose up` (a Postgres container is already running for this checkout, see docs/anti-patterns.md).

CONTEXT ON THE SUITE'S CURRENT STATE so you are not surprised: `mix test` currently has roughly 13-14 pre-existing failures confined to Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest and Letflow.IdentityMigrationTest, independently observed by ELIXIR-DEV and SECURITY-REVIEWER and attributed as pre-existing (ELIXIR-DEV stashed its changes back to HEAD and reproduced them identically). They are not yours to fix or attribute. Note that Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest spawns a nested full `mix test`, which is why it times out -- be careful that your own new test does NOT adopt that pattern.
acceptance_criteria: AC1 -- test/specs/ISS-0106.md exists and states, per WF-03's Step 4 rule, the fail-then-pass evidence explicitly: what was run against pre-fix code, what it produced, what it produces post-fix. This must cover Parts B and C via the two gate exit codes measured at main vs HEAD by you, and Part A via its new tests
AC2 -- The new test file exists, follows the placement convention of the existing mix-task test rather than a newly-invented one, and compiles

AC3 -- The MATCH path is covered by a fixture-driven test that does not hardcode this host's version, and the OTP major-only rule is covered specifically: a pinned full erlang version must MATCH a running major-only OTP release. State how the test would fail if the rule were implemented as a naive full-string comparison

AC4 -- Mismatch is covered for Elixir alone, OTP alone, and both together, with the assertion checking that BOTH the expected and the running version appear in the output, since naming both is what the decision record requires of the warning
AC5 -- The parse contract is covered: comment lines, blank lines, another tool's line, and a malformed line. State which the design says are ignored and which are reported, and assert accordingly
AC6 -- Every failure mode the design enumerates (F1..F8) has a test, and each asserts BOTH that a message is produced AND that run/1 returned :ok without raising
AC7 -- The non-suppressibility and never-raises properties are asserted rather than assumed, including that warning output goes to stderr
AC8 -- A mechanical describe+test name-length check was run over every pair in the new file, and the maximum measured length is quoted. It must be under 200 characters
AC9 -- The new tests were run and their real output quoted -- pass count, failure count. Your own tests must be green; the suite's ~13-14 pre-existing failures elsewhere are not yours
AC10 -- No source file under lib/ is modified. If the module needs a change to be testable, that is a finding to report, not a change to make
AC11 -- No test asserts a hardcoded toolchain version that would fail on a host running something other than this one. State how you ensured this

result.summary: Regression coverage for ISS-0106 written and proven fail-then-pass. PART A: 30 new ExUnit tests in test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_toolchain_test.exs (underscore filename, matching the existing test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_test_test.exs convention rather than the dotted path named in owned_modules -- AC2 requires the existing convention). At HEAD: 'Result: 30 passed', 0 failures, exit 0, 0.6s. Fail-first proven in a throwaway git worktree of main: the same file at pre-fix main gives 'Result: 0/30 passed / Failed: 30 tests' (UndefinedFunctionError, module not available), exit 2; adding ONLY lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain.ex from 9ca2071 to that worktree takes it to 30 passed. Three mutation negative controls confirm the tests are not tautological: naive full-string OTP comparison -> 17/30; -otp-NN suffix not stripped -> 24/30; warnings to stdout instead of stderr -> 11/30. PARTS B and C: no ExUnit tests written (their exit-code gates already exist); the fail-then-pass exit codes were measured directly at main vs HEAD -- 'mix format --check-formatted' exit 1 (exactly 4 files) at main, exit 0 at HEAD; 'MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors' exit 1 at main (14 'is expected on struct update' warnings), exit 0 at HEAD. ExUnit name-length check run mechanically over all 30 describe+test pairs: MAX = 75 characters ('test failure modes F7 an unavailable working directory warns and returns ok'), well under the 200-char working limit and the 255-char hard cap. All F1..F8 covered; F6 induced for real via :eisdir, F8 induced for real via a group leader that refuses the Erlang IO protocol. No file under lib/ modified in this checkout; mutants were confined to the worktree, which has been removed. mix format --check-formatted is clean at HEAD including the new file.
issues: FINDING (not a blocker, no rework requested): failure mode F7 (File.cwd/0 returning {:error, _}) has no portable external trigger. On POSIX a process can delete its own cwd; on Windows the OS refuses -- measured on this host: File.rm_rf of the cwd returns {:error, :eacces} and File.cwd/0 still returns {:ok, _}. Two other candidate inductions were probed and rejected (over-long cwd: File.cd fails :eio so the cwd never changes; invalid UTF-8 in the pin file: the parse absorbs it, which is correct behaviour). Making F7 directly inducible would need a public seam on the module (injectable path or exposed comparison), which is a design change routing through CODE-DESIGNER, not TEST-DESIGNER. T-F7 therefore attempts the real induction and asserts the real F7 block wherever the OS permits it (POSIX hosts, e.g. hetzner), and where it does not, asserts the structural guarantee the branch rests on (File.cwd() and never File.cwd!, F7 branch text present). Neither branch is a no-op and the test is not skipped. On this Windows host the structural branch was taken. Documented in test/specs/ISS-0106.md section 3.6.

NOTE: the test file is async: false and moves the VM-wide working directory around each run/1 call, because the task reads .tool-versions from the cwd and offers no path seam. The cd window is held to the single run/1 call to minimise interference with concurrent async tests. Same root cause as the F7 finding above.

NOTE on naming: handoff context.owned_modules named test/mix/tasks/letflow.check_toolchain_test.exs (dotted). The file was written as test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_toolchain_test.exs (underscored) because AC2 requires the convention of the existing mix-task test, which maps the dotted task path to underscores (letflow.check.test.ex -> letflow_check_test_test.exs). Flagged so ORCH can reconcile the registry entry.

CONTEXT (not attributed here, per the handoff): the suite's ~13-14 pre-existing failures in Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest and Letflow.IdentityMigrationTest were not investigated. The new file does not shell out to a nested mix test and does not share their failure mode.
